summary: Scanned all 10 guides, 23 blog posts and 150 long articles (EN) by script plus targeted reads. Clean on dashes, AI, brand name, fees, refund promises and residency hedging. One P0 pattern: three pages describe the agent lodgment program for "their clients" then say "ask us", which implies SVT is the agent; the what-is-a-tax-agent and DIY articles do the same by juxtaposition (P1). Fact error: DASP 65% is stated as applying to the "whole payment" in 11 places, but the tax-free component stays 0%. SEO: heavy cannibalization (7 DASP pages, DASP docs pair both at pos 53, 8 more duplicate pairs), long articles never link to the service pages, no TFN service page, most hubs lack FAQs.

findings.category: rule: implies SVT is a tax agent
findings.locator: blog-en.ts:493 "Registered tax agents have a lodgment program that can allow a later date for their clients, depending on the client's circumstances, so ask us about yours." | blog-en.ts:936-939 section "Is it later with a tax agent?": "Registered tax agents have a lodgment program that usually lets them lodge for their clients after 31 October." ... "Ask us about your own position." | batch-09.ts:823 "A registered tax agent can sometimes lodge later than that date, but only if the client was on the agent's list in time, and the timing can differ if earlier returns were still outstanding. Ask us about your own situation."
findings.problem: Each paragraph describes what a registered tax agent can do for "their clients" and then says "ask us". A reader takes this to mean SVT is the agent that has the lodgment program, which breaks the rule against saying or implying SVT is a tax agent.
findings.fix: Keep the ATO fact neutral and make the CTA about the service only. blog-en.ts:493 -> "...A late return can still be lodged. Registered tax agents have a lodgment program that can allow a later date for their clients, depending on the client's circumstances. Message us on WhatsApp with the years you worked and we confirm your price before you pay." blog-en.ts:939 -> delete "Ask us about your own position." (or "Lodge as soon as you can; the next section explains what happens if you missed it."). batch-09.ts:823 -> end at "...earlier returns were still outstanding." and drop "Ask us about your own situation."
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md lines 28-30 and SVT_BRIEF rule: never say or imply SVT IS a tax agent. Only the two approved sentences may describe the agent.

findings.category: rule: implies SVT is a tax agent (juxtaposition)
findings.locator: batch-02.ts:17 "The ATO says registered tax agents are the only people who can charge a fee to prepare and lodge your tax return... a person who takes money for doing your return must be registered." + :54 "They cannot give you a registration number you can check on the TPB register." + :75 "Check the agent on the TPB public register." followed directly by "Student Visa Tax operates under the supervision of a registered tax agent..." | batch-11.ts:840 "If you answered "yes" to any of them, a review by a registered tax agent may help." followed directly by "Student Visa Tax operates under the supervision of a registered tax agent." | batch-11.ts:551-553 "If you use a registered tax agent and contact them before the deadline, you may be able to lodge later. What to have ready for us:"
findings.problem: The checklist "check the agent on the TPB register / only registered agents may charge a fee" leads straight into the SVT sign-off and the $220/$385 fees, so the reader concludes SVT is the registered agent (or, worse, that SVT is charging without registration). Same pattern where "a registered tax agent may help" or "use a registered tax agent ... lodge later" is immediately followed by "us".
findings.fix: Put a neutral bridge sentence between the generic agent advice and the SVT paragraph, and never let "you/your agent" flow into "us". batch-02.ts end: replace the last paragraph with "Student Visa Tax operates under the supervision of a registered tax agent. Every return is reviewed and signed off by a registered tax agent before it is lodged with the ATO. Ask us on WhatsApp for the name of the supervising agent so you can check it on the TPB register yourself." batch-11.ts:840 -> "If you answered "yes" to any of them, it is worth having your return checked before it is lodged." batch-11.ts:553 -> move "What to have ready for us:" after a paragraph break that starts "Whoever lodges your return, have these ready:".
findings.evidence: Text order read from the source; brief rule on implication; ato.gov.au "registered tax agents are the only people who can charge a fee".

findings.locator: guides-en.ts:490 "If you also held a working holiday visa (417 or 462), and the payment includes super from that time, the ATO applies 65% to the whole amount." | batch-08.ts:281 answer "The 65% rate applies to the whole payment if it includes any super from contributions made while you held a 417 or 462 visa." | batch-02.ts:512 "65% applies to the whole amount." | batch-10.ts:286 "A higher rate of 65% applies to the whole payment..." | batch-08.ts:323 "Tax at 65% on the whole payment: $6,500"
findings.problem: The ATO says the tax-free component of a DASP stays at 0% for working holiday makers; 65% applies to the taxed and untaxed elements of the taxable component (all of it, not split by period). "Whole amount/whole payment" overstates the tax and contradicts the 0% tax-free line in the same articles. 11 occurrences.
findings.fix: Replace with: "If the payment includes super from contributions made while you held a 417 or 462 visa, 65% applies to the whole taxable component (both the taxed and untaxed elements). The tax-free component stays at 0%." Worked examples: add "assuming the balance is all taxed element" before "$6,500 is withheld".
findings.evidence: ATO "DASP and working holiday makers changes, FAQ" (ato.gov.au/super/apra-regulated-funds/.../dasp-and-working-holiday-makers-changes---frequently-asked-questions): "The tax-free component continues to be taxed at 0%"; 65% applies to "the taxed and untaxed elements of the taxable component".

findings.locator: blog-en.ts:644 slug "dasp-documents-and-timing" title "DASP application: documents and processing time" vs batch-08.ts:178 "dasp-documents-checklist-international-students" title "DASP paperwork for former students: certified copies explained"; batch-08.ts:276 "DASP tax for international students: usually 35%, not 65%" vs batch-02.ts:507 "Tax on super when international students leave Australia" (same H2s: "What are the DASP tax rates?", worked example, "When does the 65% rate apply?", checklist)

Seven DASP pages, none clearly the target.
findings.fix: One page per intent: (1) Rates: keep /blog/dasp-tax-rate-international-students, merge tax-on-super-withdrawal into it and 301 the old slug (zh/vi too); retitle "Tax on your DASP (departing Australia superannuation payment): 35% for students" and add a rate table (tax-free 0%, taxed element 35%, untaxed 45%, WHM 65% on taxable component). (2) Documents and timing: keep /blog/dasp-documents-and-timing as the hub, fold the certified-copies detail of dasp-documents-checklist into it and 301. (3) /superannuation stays the service page: add a "DASP tax rates" link to (1) and "documents and timing" to (2) in its first section, and link both back to /superannuation with anchor "help claiming your super".
findings.evidence: GSC export Pages + Queries sheets, 26 Oct-5 Nov 2026.

findings.locator: relatedOf(): "const same = LONG_EN.filter(x => x.category === a.category && x.slug !== a.slug) ... .slice(0, 5).map(x => `blog/${x.slug}`)"
findings.problem: The 150 long articles (most of the impressions) link only to 5 sibling long articles of the same category, plus WhatsApp. They never link to the service and hub pages: /superannuation, /abn-delivery, /pricing, /tax-residency, /medicare, /do-i-need-to-lodge, or the topic hubs in BLOG_EN. Bodies cannot carry links (types.ts forbids them). PageRank and topical signals do not flow to the four service pages, and /superannuation sits at pos 90.
findings.fix: In relatedOf(), prepend the service page for the category: Super -> "superannuation", ABN -> "abn-delivery", Medicare -> "medicare", Tax return/Deductions -> "pricing" (or "do-i-need-to-lodge"), TFN -> the TFN hub (see GEN-07), Work -> "blog/payslip-what-to-check"; then 4 siblings. Optionally add `service?: string` to LongArticle so an article can override.
findings.evidence: Code read; GuidePage.tsx renders only g.related and place.next for these pages.
